source.title: OmniJARVIS: Unified Vision-Language-Action Tokenization Enables Open-World Instruction Following Agents
source.authors: Zihao Wang; Shaofei Cai; Zhan-Cun Mu; Haowei Lin; Ceyao Zhang; Xuejie Liu; Qing Li; Anji Liu; Xiaojian Ma; Yi-Tao Liang

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling analysis to instruction-tuned vision-language-action models for Minecraft and reports validation-loss trends as training data and model scale vary.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the validation instruction-following loss scaling analysis in Section 4.6 and Figure 5. Other reported task scores, tokenizer ablations, and the Atari reward do not measure a claim version's scaling-law behavior.
record.test_reason: Section 4.6 tracks validation loss as fine-tuning data grows for 2B, 7B and 13B VLA fine-tunes in Minecraft. This is a new setting (multimodal instruction fine-tuning) bearing on V5, though no power law is fitted.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say instruction tuning 'aligns with the scaling law', with log-linear loss decrease in data. Larger VLMs lower the loss, but the 7B-to-13B gain is smaller, hinting at saturation. They stress matching data volume to model size.
record.recipe_differences: This is a fine-tuning and evaluation-loss scaling study on Minecraft multimodal interaction data, varying data amount and VLM size; it is not a language-model pretraining sweep or a compute-optimal allocation experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling trend is considered across different model sizes; the authors note that gains from 7B to 13B are less pronounced than from 2B to 7B.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger behavior codebooks (e8 to e14) give higher average reward and lower FSD (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discrete action-tokenizer codebook size improves agent performance.

record.problems: The loss curves are shown in a figure without exact loss values or stated data-scale amounts in the text. The study reports correlations and a qualitative log-linear trend, but does not fit explicit power-law exponents or assess prediction from smaller runs to much larger runs.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly measure a version of the claim; task-success and question-answering evaluations, tokenizer ablations, and Atari transfer results are not scaling-law measurements.

untested.parts: Extrapolation from small to large runs.
Shape effects at fixed parameter count.
Explicit power-law fit or exponents in fine-tuning; other modalities; repeated data; a clean model-size law with base models held constant.
Downstream task performance versus scale (task scores were not reported by scale).

missing.what: Model-size comparison of validation loss across 2B, 7B and 13B: 7B clearly below 2B, 13B only slightly below 7B.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is thin: a figure with three curves, unstated data amounts and no fitted exponents. Model sizes confound base-model family and vision tokenizer. The text gives about 1T total training tokens, but the components sum to about 1B, an internal inconsistency. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation at fixed compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

The study reports scaling in one Minecraft interaction-data fine-tuning setting, but does not fit or establish the same power-law form explicitly, and does not test image/video scaling broadly, repeated data, or other training regimes.
Downstream task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices, and systematic bending from power laws.

rows.subject: OmniJARVIS-2B
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned from LLaVA-2B with Gemma-2B language models
rows.operation_detail: Monitored validation instruction-following loss as training-data amount increased.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation reported for evaluation loss across data scales
rows.note: The authors state that all model curves show a log-linear decrease in evaluation loss as data scale increases.
rows.check: The value is a Pearson coefficient whose fit is unstated, probably loss against log data. Loss falls log-linearly, not as an explicit power law. Data amounts and loss values are unstated. No baseline.

rows.subject: OmniJARVIS-7B
rows.operation_detail: Monitored validation instruction-following loss as training-data amount increased.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation reported for evaluation loss across data scales
rows.note: The authors state that all model curves show a log-linear decrease in evaluation loss as data scale increases; they report significantly lower losses for 7B than 2B.
rows.check: Same as r1: Pearson coefficient of an unstated fit, log-linear rather than a fitted power law, data amounts unstated.

rows.subject: OmniJARVIS-13B
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned from LLaVA-13B with LLaMA2-13B language models
rows.operation_detail: Monitored validation instruction-following loss as training-data amount increased.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation reported for evaluation loss across data scales
rows.note: The authors state that all model curves show a log-linear decrease in evaluation loss as data scale increases; they describe the improvement over 7B as less pronounced and suggest possible saturation.
rows.check: Same as r1. The 7B-to-13B saturation remark concerns model size, not this data-scaling row; it belongs in a separate model-size row.

relationships.condition: Data scaling of validation loss when fine-tuning OmniJARVIS 2B, 7B and 13B on Minecraft interaction data
relationships.reason: Loss falls log-linearly with data, Pearson 0.9991/0.9999/0.9989 (r1–r3). The power-law form itself is not fitted, so support is weak.
relationships.display_finding: Validation loss fell log-linearly with data, with reported Pearson correlations of 0.9991, 0.9999 and 0.9989 for 2B, 7B and 13B models, without fitting the power-law form.

relationships.condition: Model-size scaling 7B to 13B (text only, no row)
relationships.reason: Authors report a much smaller loss gain from 7B to 13B than from 2B to 7B and hint at saturation. This rests on the text; base-model families differ (Gemma, Vicuna, LLaMA2).
relationships.display_finding: Loss improved much less from 7B to 13B than from 2B to 7B, although base-model families differed.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: OmniJARVIS 2B, 7B, and 13B across the tested data scales
reader_labels.reason: Evaluation loss decreases as data scale increases; the reported Pearson correlations are 0.9991, 0.9999, and 0.9989 (r1–r3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The authors say the improvement is less pronounced and may be approaching saturation, qualifying the scaling trend at larger model size (r2–r3).
